title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Make polite requests, ask favours, invite and be invited, accept or decline gracefully, and offer good wishes.
intro:
Telugu politeness relies less on 'please' than on **verb forms**: a polite request is usually a question in the plural, *ఇస్తారా?* ('will you give?'), softened with *కొంచెం* (a little) and *అండి*. Blessings and wishes use the *-ఆలి* form: *మీరు బాగుండాలి* (may you be well).

An important Telugu concept is **మొహమాటం** (mohamāṭam): the reluctance to impose, ask or accept. Hosts will press food on you precisely to overcome it, and *మొహమాటం వద్దు!* ('no need to be shy!') is a phrase you will hear often.

vocab.note: Colloquially సాయం (sāyam); to help: సహాయం చేయు.

vocab.en: to wait for, look forward to
to put, place; to serve; to do for someone
vocab.note: After -i form: చేసి పెట్టు, do for (someone).

phrases.en: Come to our place for a meal.
If it's no trouble for you...
Here you are, a small gift.
Sorry, I can't come this time.

grammar.title: Polite requests: 'will you...?', 'could you...?'
grammar.body:
A bare command, even with *-ండి*, can sound abrupt for a favour. Softer options, from neutral to most polite:
• **Polite imperative + కొంచెం**: *కొంచెం ఆగండి* (wait a moment, please).
• **Non-past question** 'will you?': *ఇస్తారా?* (will you give?), *చెప్తారా?* (will you tell?).
• **Ability question** 'could you?': *చేయగలరా?* (could you do?), more formal.
• **Benefactive -ఇ పెట్టు** 'do it for me': *చదివి పెడతారా?* (would you read it for me?).

Add **అండి** at the end for extra respect, and **దయచేసి** in writing or formal speech. For 'please don't', use **-కండి**: *పొగ తాగకండి*.

examples.en: Could you help me a little?
Would you fill in this form for me, please?

grammar.title: Wishes, blessings and declining
grammar.body:
The **-ఆలి** form you know as 'must' also expresses **wishes and blessings** (an optative): *మీరు బాగుండాలి* (may you be well), *మీ కోరికలు తీరాలి* (may your wishes be fulfilled). Elders bless the young with *నూరేళ్ళు చల్లగా ఉండాలి* ('may you live a hundred cool [peaceful] years').

**'It would be nice if'**: conditional **-తే** + *బాగుంటుంది*: *మీరు వస్తే బాగుంటుంది*.

**Declining** is done indirectly: an apology + 'can't' (*క్షమించండి, రాలేను*), *ఈసారి కుదరదు* (it won't work out this time), or *చూద్దాం* (we'll see). When refusing food, *చాలు, చాలు!* with a hand over the plate.

examples.en: May you live a long and happy life.
It would be nice if you came.
Don't be shy, have some more.
Sorry, it won't work out this time.

dialogue.title: A house-warming invitation
dialogue.setting: Vasantha visits her neighbour Kamala to invite her to her new home's house-warming.

lines.speaker: Vasantha
lines.native: కమల గారూ, నమస్కారం. వచ్చే ఆదివారం మా గృహప్రవేశం. మీరు కుటుంబంతో తప్పకుండా రావాలి.
lines.roman: kamala gārū, namaskāram. vachchē ādivāram mā gruhapravēsham. mīru kuṭumbamtō tappakuṇḍā rāvāli.
lines.en: Kamala garu, hello. Next Sunday is our house-warming. You must come with your family.

lines.speaker: Kamala
lines.en: Congratulations! We'll definitely come. What time?

lines.speaker: Vasantha
lines.native: పొద్దున్న పూజ, మధ్యాహ్నం భోజనం. పదకొండు గంటలకల్లా రండి.
lines.roman: poddunna pūja, madhyānnam bhōjanam. padakoṇḍu gaṇṭalakallā raṇḍi.
lines.en: The puja is in the morning, lunch at midday. Please come by eleven.

lines.speaker: Kamala
lines.native: సరే. ఏమైనా సహాయం కావాలా? ఏమైనా చేసి పెట్టనా?
lines.roman: sarē. ēmainā sahāyam kāvālā? ēmainā chēsi peṭṭanā?
lines.en: Okay. Do you need any help? Shall I make something for you?

lines.speaker: Vasantha
lines.native: మీరు వస్తే చాలు. కానీ మొహమాటం లేకుండా అడుగుతున్నాను, మీ దగ్గర పెద్ద గిన్నెలు ఉంటే ఇవ్వగలరా?
lines.roman: mīru vastē chālu. kānī mohamāṭam lēkuṇḍā aḍugutunnānu, mī daggara pedda ginnelu uṇṭē ivvagalarā?
lines.en: Your coming is enough. But I'll ask without hesitation: if you have some big cooking pots, could you lend them?

lines.speaker: Kamala
lines.en: Oh, of course! I'll send them tomorrow itself.

lines.speaker: Vasantha
lines.native: చాలా థాంక్స్ అండి. మీ సహాయం మర్చిపోలేను.
lines.roman: chālā thāṅks aṇḍi. mī sahāyam marchipōlēnu.
lines.en: Thank you so much. I won't forget your help.

lines.speaker: Kamala
lines.native: ఇందులో ఏముంది! ఇరుగుపొరుగు అంటే అంతే కదా.
lines.roman: indulō ēmundi! iruguporugu aṇṭē antē kadā.
lines.en: It's nothing! That's what neighbours are for.

culture: Invitations to weddings and house-warmings are delivered **in person**, often with turmeric-marked cards, *kumkum* and a few betel leaves; a phone call alone can seem casual for close relations. Guests rarely arrive empty-handed (fruit or sweets are standard), and hosts may offer departing women *పసుపు కుంకుమ* and a blouse-piece as a mark of respect. Expect hosts to insist on second and third helpings; this *బలవంతం* is hospitality, not pressure.
